explanations: inventory_reserve checks inv->available before taking the mutex. Two threads can both see enough seats (for example 2 left, each asking for 2), then acquire the lock in turn and each subtract, driving available negative and overselling the flight. The check and the decrement must happen under the same lock acquisition. Everything else is guarded: the hold table scan, the decrement, release and inventory_available all hold the mutex.

The id is taken inside the critical section, so every access to the counter is already serialized by inv->lock; the atomic is redundant but harmless. Another option is wrong because the mutex does cover that line. Another option is wrong: the atomic does not order anything relative to the slot writes. Another option is wrong: lock and unlock do provide the needed ordering.

The first call finds an active hold with that id, adds its seats back, marks the slot inactive and returns the seat count. The second finds no active hold with id 7 and returns 0 without modifying available, so a double release is harmless. Nothing blocks and there is no thread-ownership check.

The slot scan finds no inactive entry, so the code unlocks the mutex and returns RESERVE_HOLD_TABLE_FULL before touching inv->available. The sold-out code comes only from the seat comparison, no hold is overwritten, and nothing waits: the mutex is released before returning.
